Values come from %1$s. A value shown as NO DATA was not available or could not be read; the app never estimates it. Higher solar flux generally helps the higher HF bands (15 m and up). A K-index of 5 or more means a geomagnetic storm, which often degrades HF and polar paths. These are general indicators, not a forecast for a specific path.

A dashboard for licensed radio amateurs working in the Chornobyl region: public repeater information, DMR parameters, band and digital mode references, UTC and local clocks, propagation data, weather and drone flight weather, and the history of the Exclusion Zone. It is not a navigator and is not intended for any military purpose.

Repeaters come from the public HearHam.live directory (hearham.com): entries listed as operational within 300 km of Chornobyl, retrieved on 2026-09-28. A listing does not prove that a repeater is on air, so their status is unknown. Talkgroups come from BrandMeister public documentation. Check before use.
Any https JSON catalog you enter under Settings > Data source. Entries without a stated source are rejected. The app shows each entry\'s source.
Bundled general reference based on the IARU Region 1 band plan overview and the projects\' official sites. Verify against your national allocation plan.

Your position is used to show you on the map, to sort distances and to compute sun times. It is uploaded only if you choose \"My location\" as the weather place, and then rounded to about 10 km before it is sent to Open-Meteo. Location is requested only when you tap something that needs it. The app sends no analytics. Network requests go only to the sources listed above.

For civilian amateur radio use only. The app has no function to intercept or decode private or protected communications, search for military frequencies, locate military sites, or track people. The map shows only public civilian and historical landmarks. The drone section rates weather only and is not a flight permission; follow martial-law rules and the Exclusion Zone access rules. Transmit only where your license and national rules allow it.

Ukraine is under martial law. Civilian drone flights are restricted and generally need prior approval from the military administration of the region. The Chornobyl Exclusion Zone is a restricted area: entering it and flying there need official permission from the State Agency on Exclusion Zone Management. Never fly near critical infrastructure, military units, rescue operations or people who have not agreed to it. Keep the drone in sight. This app only rates the weather and never tells you that a flight is permitted. Rules change: check the current ones before every flight.

Conservative guidance for small quads: wind up to %1$s m/s is good, above %2$s m/s no-go; gusts up to %3$s m/s good, above %4$s m/s no-go; wind at 80 m up to %5$s m/s good, above %6$s m/s no-go. Any rain or snow, thunderstorms, fog, frost and darkness lower the rating. The worst factor decides. Without wind data there is no rating. Check your drone\'s own limits.

Common analog VTX channels. Without an amateur license use only channels in the 5725-5875 MHz short-range-device band at low power (typically 25 mW EIRP). The 5650-5850 MHz amateur band needs a license and your call sign.

2.4 GHz (ELRS, other RC systems) is license-exempt with power limits. 868 MHz long-range links must stay within the short-range-device sub-bands and their duty-cycle limits. 433 MHz is in the 70 cm amateur band and needs a license. 915 MHz is a US band and is not license-exempt in Ukraine or the EU. Interference with other services is never allowed.

When the K-index reaches 5 or more, GNSS positions can drift and compasses can be disturbed. Return-to-home and position hold may become unreliable. Calibrate the compass away from metal and power lines.

1. Permissions for this place and time are in hand. 2. Weather and wind checked, including gusts. 3. Props, frame, antennas and camera undamaged and tight. 4. Batteries charged, warm and not puffed. 5. Failsafe and return-to-home tested; GNSS fix acquired if used. 6. Video channel free and legal; no one else on it. 7. Take-off area clear of people, wires and trees. 8. A spotter is with you when flying FPV goggles.

Below 5 °C LiPo cells lose capacity and voltage sags under load: keep packs warm until take-off and land earlier. Never charge cold, damaged or puffed packs. Charge on a fireproof surface, never unattended, and store at storage voltage (about 3.8 V per cell).

Transmitting is banned under martial law

Ukraine has prohibited the operation of amateur transmitting stations since 2022 (Presidential Decrees No. 133/2022, 259/2022 and 341/2022). The repeaters listed here may be off air. Do not transmit until the ban is lifted; check the current rules with the Ukrainian Amateur Radio League (UARL) and NCEC.
Measured dose rates near the Zone (Safecast)

These are volunteer measurements, not official monitoring. They can be old, incomplete or wrong, and levels in the Zone change a lot over a few meters. Do not use this map to decide whether a place is safe. Entering the Exclusion Zone needs an official permit.
Volunteer data, not a safety assessment. The Exclusion Zone can be entered only with an official permit.

The colors only group the numbers; they are not safety limits. For comparison, natural background gamma radiation in most places is roughly 0.05 to 0.3 µSv/h.

Readings come from %1$s, a volunteer network. The app always asks for the area around the power plant and never sends your position. Readings from the last year are grouped into cells of about 2 km and the median is shown, so single survey tracks do not appear and nothing about who took a reading is kept. Values given in counts per minute (CPM) are converted with 334 CPM per µSv/h (bGeigie Nano), so they are estimates; other detectors differ. The data is not verified by any authority.
